clue.text: Account in which a trio of figures are detailed?

definitions.text: Account in which a trio of figures are detailed?

blocks.clueFragment: Account in which a trio of figures are detailed?
blocks.note: surface reading: a report describing three people in close detail
setter's reading: de-tailed, having their tails cut off, as happens to three creatures in a well-known nursery rhyme

explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' looks like 'described minutely' but splits as de-tailed: the farmer's wife cuts off the tails of the three sightless rodents in the rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery rhyme is a short story, or account, in which a carving knife removes the tails of three small creatures.

clue.text: Evil cheat desecrated font

indicators.note: something desecrated has been violated and spoiled, so these letters are wrecked and rebuilt

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A wicked cheat has defiled a baptismal font in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Font' suggests a church basin, which fits 'desecrated', but here it means a typeface.
explanation.definitionFit: Helvetica is a widely used sans-serif typeface, an example of a font in typography.

clue.text: Like youngster's first pint in place by the Med

indicators.note: first tells us to keep only the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: eg, for example, introduces something alike
the initial letter of youngster
PT is the standard abbreviation for pint

explanation.surface: A teenager has a first pint of beer in a Mediterranean resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt is a country on the southeastern shore of the Mediterranean Sea, a place beside it.

clue.text: Direction and date announced to arrive at vast body of water

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so we want words that sound like the ones clued

blocks.note: a bearing is a compass direction
to see someone is to date them

explanation.surface: Someone is told a heading and a day on which to reach a great ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bering Sea is the large northern arm of the Pacific between Alaska and Siberia, a huge expanse of water.

clue.text: Dodgy info; Trump’s dropping behind otherwise

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or not right, so the letters are put in another order
dropping means letting go of something, so one word loses part of itself

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
taken as written
a rump is a backside, removed from the previous word

explanation.surface: Unreliable information, with Trump falling behind in the polls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' looks like a position word, but it is a noun: TRUMP drops its RUMP, leaving T.
explanation.definitionFit: If not is a phrase used to introduce an alternative, the same sense as otherwise or else.

clue.text: Insensitive, possibly, Donald’s offering things that won’t work

blocks.note: dead can mean numb, without feeling, one possible sense of insensitive
Donald Duck, the cartoon character, with the possessive s

explanation.surface: A tactless man named Donald puts forward proposals that will fail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Donald' suggests a politician, but it is Disney's Donald Duck.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead duck is an idiom for a plan or person certain to fail, so dead ducks are failures.

clue.text: I will be given a large quantity: perfect

blocks.note: taken as written
as in a great deal

explanation.surface: Someone receives a big amount of something and finds it just right.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal as an adjective describes something flawless or exactly as wished, a synonym for perfect.

clue.text: Alarmingly silent son becomes soldier

indicators.note: alarmingly suggests something disturbed and thrown into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A worryingly quiet son decides to join the army.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist is to sign up for military service, so a person who enlists turns into a member of the army.

clue.text: Oliver’s family dances

blocks.note: first meaning: the relatives of Dickens's orphan hero, surname included
second meaning: the 1960s rock-and-roll dance, plural

explanation.surface: The relatives of a boy called Oliver are dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver is Dickens's orphan, whose surname pluralised names his family.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Twist's relatives would be the Twists, and the twist is a vigorous 1960s dance.

clue.text: Not a byelaw broken by archbishop

indicators.note: not means without, so the following little word is taken away
something broken is smashed into pieces that can be put together differently

blocks.note: taken as written, then removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: An archbishop is accused of breaking a local regulation.
explanation.definitionFit: Justin Welby served as Archbishop of Canterbury, head of the Church of England, from 2013 to 2025.

clue.text: To evoke old memory, emulate town crier

blocks.note: first meaning: to seem familiar, to stir a recollection
second meaning: to do what a public announcer does with a handbell

explanation.surface: Someone recalls the past by copying the old official who shouted the news.
explanation.walkthrough: A town crier was the official who walked the streets calling out news, swinging a handbell.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means something feels familiar, and literally it describes sounding a handbell as a town crier did.

clue.text: Son taking protein didn't get up

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son
leptin is a protein hormone that regulates appetite

explanation.surface: A son on a protein diet stayed in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To sleep in is a phrasal verb for staying in bed later than usual, past the normal rising time.

clue.text: Unprofessional hairdresser half-smiles, makes uncertain movements

indicators.note: half tells us to keep only one half of the word that follows

blocks.note: Sweeney Todd, the murderous demon barber of Fleet Street
the back half of this six-letter word

explanation.surface: A clumsy hairdresser gives a weak smile and moves hesitantly.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweeney Todd is the fictional barber who murdered his customers, hardly professional conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: To toddle is to walk with short unsteady steps, as a small child does, which fits wobbly movement.

clue.text: Bird who wrote satire

blocks.note: first meaning: the fast-flying summer migrant
second meaning: Jonathan, the Irish satirist behind Gulliver's Travels

explanation.surface: A bird that apparently wrote satire.
explanation.definitionFit: The swift is a fast aerial bird, and Jonathan Swift wrote Gulliver's Travels and A Modest Proposal.

clue.text: Chinese way of thinking is superior to every single European PM

blocks.note: the Tao, the way, central to Taoist philosophy
taken as written
each means every one individually

explanation.surface: A Chinese philosophy is claimed to outrank every European prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, superior to means placed above, so the first pieces sit on top of the last.
explanation.definitionFit: Taoiseach is the title of the Irish head of government, the prime minister of Ireland, a European country.

clue.text: Petitions with legal process stowed in large containers

indicators.note: stowed in means packed inside, so one word is placed within the other

blocks.note: a suit is a petition or appeal, as in pressing one's suit
a case is a lawsuit

explanation.surface: Legal petitions and court papers are packed away in big boxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Suitcases are large travelling bags with a handle, used for carrying clothes, so they are luggage containers.

clue.text: Buy goofier backless pants please

indicators.note: backless means lacking a back, so the word loses its final letter
pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are poor and must be reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, before losing its end

explanation.surface: A plea to buy sillier trousers cut low at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like trousers (or underwear in Britain), but it is slang for rubbish, signalling the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: I beg of you is an earnest plea, used like please when asking someone to do something.

clue.text: Conceited fellow’s keen to get a Guinness

blocks.note: keen and smart both mean sharp or quick-witted
Sir Alec Guinness, the actor

explanation.surface: A vain man is eager for a pint of stout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A Guinness' suggests the Irish stout; it is the actor Alec Guinness, so the first name is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A smart alec is an irritating know-it-all who thinks he is cleverer than everyone, a conceited man.

clue.text: The Spanish are heartlessly appropriating legendary Kazakh: it’s complicated

indicators.note: heartlessly means with the middle removed, so only the outside letters of the word are kept
appropriating means taking possession of, so the letters seize and hold another word

blocks.note: el is the Spanish masculine definite article
the outer letters of this three-letter word
Borat, Sacha Baron Cohen's spoof Kazakh journalist

explanation.surface: Spaniards are ruthlessly taking over a famous Kazakh character, and the situation is messy.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaborate as an adjective describes something intricate and detailed, with many parts, close in sense to complicated.

clue.text: ‘Turkey’s head,’ butcher groaned

indicators.note: to butcher something is to hack it apart, so the letters are chopped up and rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A butcher grumbles about the head of a turkey bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turkey's head' suggests the bird at a butcher's, but it is the country's leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Recep Tayyip Erdogan has led Turkey as prime minister and then president, its head of state.

clue.text: Part of flight in fastest Airbus

indicators.note: in means contained within, so the letters lie inside the words that follow

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A section of a journey aboard the quickest passenger jet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' and 'Airbus' suggest air travel, but the flight is a set of steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of stairs is a series of steps, so one step is a single part of that flight.

clue.text: Well-mannered denizen muffling flush

indicators.note: muffling means wrapping up and covering, so the wanted letters are enclosed by the words

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A polite local resident hides his embarrassment as he blushes.
explanation.definitionFit: To flush is to go red in the face, from embarrassment or heat, the same as to blush.

clue.text: Place that attracts interest

blocks.note: first meaning: to put something down, a verb
second meaning: money lodged in a bank that earns interest

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a description of a tourist spot; 'interest' is the money a bank pays.
explanation.definitionFit: To deposit is to set something down, and a bank deposit is a sum saved that earns interest payments.

clue.text: Laid up, poorly, missing date with a dish

indicators.note: poorly means in bad shape, so the letters are reshaped into a new order
missing means lacking, so a letter is taken out

blocks.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for date, removed

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in bed with illness misses a date and eats a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilau is a rice dish cooked in stock with spices, common in South Asian and Middle Eastern cooking.

clue.text: Bat, seen as it sleeps, by cat

indicators.note: a bat sleeps hanging upside down, so in a down clue the word is turned the other way

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bat, noticed sleeping, beside a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: Bats roost head downwards, which in a down entry flips the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabby is a domestic cat with a striped or mottled coat, a common example of a cat.

clue.text: Excluded slang for ‘paw’ in large lexicographic work

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one word sits within the other

blocks.note: mitt is informal for a hand
the Oxford English Dictionary

explanation.surface: A slang word for a hand was left out of a big dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Omitted means left out or not included, a direct synonym of excluded.

clue.text: To be understood, with seconds to spare, finish drawing

indicators.note: to spare means left over and discarded, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: to sink in is for an idea to be grasped
S is the abbreviation for second, plural for both occurrences

explanation.surface: A sketch must be grasped and completed with a few seconds left over.
explanation.walkthrough: Both S's go, the second abbreviation once for each occurrence.
explanation.definitionFit: To ink in is to go over pencil lines in ink, the final stage of completing a drawing.

clue.text: Almost always taking bass in lively song

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is cut off
taking means adding on, so another piece joins the end
in means placed inside, so what comes before goes within the next word

blocks.note: taken as written before being shortened
B is the abbreviation for bass in music
gay in its older sense of merry and lively

explanation.surface: A cheerful song that nearly always involves a bass singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Galway Bay is a famous Irish ballad, popularised by Bing Crosby, named after the bay on Ireland's west coast.

clue.text: Singer with some frisky Lieder

indicators.note: some means a portion, so only part of the following words is used

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A vocalist performs some playful German art songs.
explanation.walkthrough: Lieder are German art songs, which nudges towards classical singers.
explanation.definitionFit: Kylie Minogue is an Australian pop star, known by her first name alone, a singer of hits.

clue.text: Nice bun that guy bolts as a guilty pleasure

indicators.note: bolts means gobbles hastily, and food wolfed down gets thoroughly churned

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man wolfs down a tasty cake as an indulgent treat.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is also the old cream-cake advertising slogan, which fits the bun.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes something enjoyable yet slightly wicked, exactly what a guilty pleasure is.
